objects.original: A compact-state process X with measurable time slices and a.e. continuous paths, an ambient C² scalar test, dyadic squared-increment sums, their real-valued in-measure limit Q, and Taylor residual sums.
objects.reconstructed: Finite measure space (Omega,m,mu); locally compact real normed space E with its Borel measurable structure; compact K⊆E; f:E→R; K-valued stochastic path X; real random variable Q.

domains.original: Finite measure μ; locally compact real normed E with its Borel measurable structure; compact subtype K; X:ℝ≥0→Ω→K and fixed T>0; Q:Ω→ℝ.
domains.reconstructed: E is a normed additive commutative group and real normed vector space, locally compact, with measurable and Borel-space instances. T>0 is a nonnegative real. X:[0,infinity)×Omega→K (subtype), Q:Omega→R.

assumptions.original: The sample space Ω carries a finite measure μ. E is a locally compact real normed space with its Borel measurable structure. K⊆E is compact. f:E→ℝ is C² at every point of K. Each time evaluation of the K-valued process X is measurable. Its paths are continuous on the specified compact time domain for μ-almost every sample. T>0, X is defined at all nonnegative times and has almost-sure continuous paths on [0,T]. The dyadic sums of squared increments converge in measure to Q:Ω→ℝ.
assumptions.reconstructed: Assumptions: mu finite; K compact; f is C² at each point of K in E. For every t≥0, X(t,·) is measurable into K. For mu-a.e. omega, t↦X(t,omega) is continuous on [0,T]. With t_i^n=iT/2^n and Delta_i^n X=X(t_{i+1}^n)-X(t_i^n) interpreted in E, ∑_{i=0}^{2^n-1}||Delta_i^n X||² converges in mu-measure to Q as n→infinity. No separate measurability or integrability hypothesis on Q is written.

conclusion.original: For a compact-state process on [0,T], the sums of second-order Taylor residuals over the dyadic grids converge in measure to zero whenever the sums of squared increments converge in measure to a real-valued Q. Formula: \sum_{i<2^n}R_f(X_{iT/2^n},X_{(i+1)T/2^n}-X_{iT/2^n})\xrightarrow{\mu}0.
conclusion.reconstructed: Conclusion: Define R_f(x,v)=f(x+v)-f(x)-Df(x)[v]-(1/2)D²f(x)[v,v]. Then omega↦∑_{i=0}^{2^n-1}R_f(X(t_i^n,omega),Delta_i^n X(omega)) converges in mu-measure to the identically zero function.

quantifiers.original: For every listed compact-state process and supplied Q, convergence in measure of dyadic squared-increment sums implies convergence in measure of the dyadic residual sums to zero.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Quantifier order: For arbitrary listed data satisfying the assumptions, convergence in measure of the dyadic squared-increment sums to the supplied Q implies convergence in measure of the dyadic second-order Taylor-remainder sums to zero.

scopes.original: Fixed positive horizon, dyadic grids, in-measure convergence only. Continuity is a.e. on [0,T], slices measurable for every nonnegative time; no extra measurability or integrability of Q is assumed.
scopes.reconstructed: Scope: One fixed positive horizon; dyadic mesh; convergence in measure only, not an asserted L¹ or almost-sure convergence. Derivatives are ambient Frechet derivatives; x+v need not independently be constrained by a neighborhood assumption.

constant_dependencies.original: Q is a supplied finite real value at every sample, subject only to the displayed convergence; no rate or constant is selected.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Constant dependencies: Q is supplied, arbitrary subject to the stated convergence; no rate or uniform constant is asserted.
